title: Fix eval/output variance caused by latency-based temperature scaling
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: A recent change to the smart-routing/latency-scaling feature introduced a per-request sampling parameter adjustment that unintentionally altered output distributions for a subset of customers. The change increased effective temperature for requests routed through the latency-scaling path and caused two customer-facing failures: (1) longer candidate tail generation (more hallucinations) that failed customer eval suites, and (2) inconsistent stop token behavior where trailing delimiters were not honored in a small fraction of responses. Both effects led to evaluation regressions seen by multiple hosted and Dedicated customers and one Private deployment escalation (CUST-4492).

Root cause: A precedence bug in the routing layer merged the latency-scaling multiplier with per-tenant overrides. For tenants marked for the latency fast-path the multiplier was applied unconditionally to the internal sampling params (temperature and top_p). The code path did not respect explicit request-level stop token lists when merging fallback stopseq configs, causing incompatible stop tokens to be used for certain model variants.

Scope: Observed regressions across Hosted API (2 customers), Dedicated pools (3 customers), and one Private deployment. Regression window: code deployed 2026-02-28 03:20 UTC; first customer report 2026-02-28 11:15 UTC.

Immediate mitigations taken:
- Rolled back the latency-scaling change in hosted runtime for all high-traffic regions within 2 hours (hotfix: infra rollback tag v1.22-rc.3 -> v1.21.9).
- Applied a targeted override for affected Dedicated pools to disable latency multiplier via admin policy patch (policy ID: POL-780).
- For Private customer CUST-4492 provided a config snippet and assisted on-site to set sampling_override: false; client received a 2-hour patch and validation run.

Permanent fix plan (current work):
1) Patch routing merge logic to ensure explicit per-request sampling and stop tokens have precedence over latency/route-level modifiers. (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2345)
2) Add an integration test that runs canonical customer evals through both fast-path and slow-path routing with deterministic seeds to detect distribution shifts.
3) Add invariants in the runtime that prevent applying temperature_multiplier > 1.0 when the request headers include an explicit temperature/top_p or explicit stop tokens.
4) Backfill historical alerts: create a metric that tracks sampling param deltas post-routing and alert if sample params change by > 10% relative to request-specified values.
5) Release runtime-1.22.1 with the fix and new regression tests.

Customer comms & postmortem: We committed to a timeline with impacted customers: short-term rollback + validation within 48 hours, permanent fix within 2 weeks, and a follow-up postmortem. Postmortem draft: confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/ENG-15823+-+Latency+sampling+regression.

Notes: This ticket captures cross-env remediation (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). There are follow-on items to improve canarying of routing feature flags and to add deterministic evals to the CI matrix.
